The raw_merchants table has 46 rows but only 40 distinct merchant_ids. Six merchant_ids appear twice, and the two copies are identical in every column. The join in gold_mcc_daily therefore fans out and inflates the counts (5317 vs 4582). Deduplicating silver_merchants fixes this. Because the duplicate copies are fully identical, SELECT DISTINCT is safe and there is no ambiguity about which row to keep. Each merchant_id then maps to one mcc. Check on the numbers: 5317 − 4582 = 735 extra rows, which is plausible for 6 duplicated merchants among 40. silver_merchants should keep the same columns (merchant_id, mcc). Nothing else needs to change. gold_merchant_daily does not use the merchants table. gold_region_daily joins customers, which are unique.
